title: The Two Pots
summary: Two different pots near a river must decide whether to enter the water together.
coverScene: A clay pot and a metal pot float together down a calm green river.

One bright day, the metal pot looked at the other pot and suggested a long journey down the stream.

However, the metal pot promised that he would stay close and protect his friend.
With that promise, both pots entered the water and began to float along.
The current was gentle, and they moved together across the bright surface.
After some time, the river became fast and rough near a narrow area of stones.
The metal pot tried to swim closer, but the heavy water pushed them apart.
The pot was pulled hard against a sharp stone in the river.
Because the material was weak, the sudden force broke the little pot into many pieces immediately.
The metal pot could not save his friend from the danger.
Although the metal pot tried to reach the broken pieces, it was already too late.
The pot sank deep down into the dark water and disappeared forever.

A smart person knows his own limits and avoids bad risks.
Real safety comes from understanding what you can and cannot do.

sentences.text: Long ago, beside the winding banks of a great and restless river, two vessels shared a quiet dwelling. One was fashioned from fragile earthenware, shaped by human hands and baked under the soft glow of an open fire. The other was forged from stern, unyielding metal, heavy with the dense weight of its own substance. Though they lived in close proximity, their natures could not have been more distinct. The earthen pot possessed a delicate beauty, light and graceful, yet acutely vulnerable to the slightest blow. The metal vessel stood proud and dark, indifferent to the common hazards that troubled its fragile companion.

One particularly bright morning, when the sunlight danced across the glassy surface of the water, the metal pot cast its gaze toward the flowing stream. It proposed a grand adventure, suggesting that they embark on a long journey down the current to see the distant lands. The earthen vessel felt a sudden tremor of hesitation ripple through its hollow core. It knew too well that water was both its cradle and its executioner, capable of shattering its fragile shell with a single careless impact. Yet the metal pot pressed the invitation with absolute confidence, offering a solemn promise of protection. It vowed to remain close at hand, shielding its companion from every hazard the river might present.

Reassured by this steadfast pledge, the earthen pot allowed itself to be coaxed toward the sloping bank. Together, they slid into the cool embrace of the current, abandoning the safety of the shore for the unpredictable depths. At first, the journey was a gentle pastoral dream. The river carried them forward with a smooth, benevolent grace, their rounded bodies bobbing in gentle synchronization across the sunlit ripples. The earthen pot began to shed its initial dread, lulled into a false sense of security by the tranquil rhythm of the voyage. It marvelled at the shifting landscape of green reeds and overhanging branches, believing fully in the protective shadow of its metallic friend.

Not far downstream, however, the character of the river began to shift with subtle menace. The banks drew closer together, squeezing the vast volume of water into a narrow, stone choked gorge where the current quickened its pace. The gentle drift transformed into a turbulent rush, churning white against jagged boulders that broke the surface like the teeth of a sleeping beast. Panic seized the earthen pot as the water battered its sides with escalating fury. The metal pot, realizing the sudden peril, attempted to swim closer to fulfill its generous promise. Yet the heavy, rushing water drove a wedge between them, pushing the companions apart with merciless indifference.

Caught in the swirling vortex, the light earthen vessel was hurled violently toward a sharp, protruding rock. Because its material was fundamentally frail, the sudden and brutal impact proved catastrophic. In a fraction of a second, the earthen pot fractured into a multitude of useless shards, scattering across the churning foam. The metal pot could do nothing to arrest the tragedy unfolding before its eyes. It fought desperately against the current, striving to reach the spot where its companion had vanished, but it was already far too late. Burdened by its own dense composition and overwhelmed by the force of the water, the metal pot sank deep into the dark, silent depths, disappearing forever from the light of day.

This ancient misfortune has echoed through generations, serving as a solemn reminder that unequal companionships carry inherent perils. If an individual lacks the fortitude to withstand adversity, that person must exercise extreme caution regarding whom they choose to trust. A wise person recognizes personal limitations with clear vision, steadfastly avoiding dangerous situations born of vanity or misplaced ambition. True security is never found in the grand promises of others, but rather in a sober understanding of one own capacity. For centuries, elders have shared this narrative with the young, ensuring that the lesson is learned before the storms of life arrive.

Many families across the country adopted this tale as a cornerstone of early instruction. If the metal pot had not initiated the journey, the earthen vessel would have remained undisturbed in its safety. Yet the fatal flaw lay in the blind trust placed upon a promise that could not withstand the reality of the river. We are thus reminded of the danger of attempting to mimic the strength of those who are fundamentally different from ourselves. Powerful friends, no matter how sincere their intentions, may inadvertently create ruin for those whose constitution is far more delicate. Every school curriculum and domestic circle has echoed this wisdom to temper youthful recklessness.

Consider once more the distinct properties of the two vessels that entered the stream. If the weaker pot had been forged from the same enduring metal, the narrative would have reached a very different conclusion. Both companions would have braved the churning rapids, emerging victorious at the mouth of the great river. Instead, the inherent weakness of the material crumbled beneath the relentless pressure of the heavy current. This event illustrates the undeniable truth that different beings possess vastly different capabilities. No one should ever attempt tasks that exceed the natural limits of their mind or body.

To live a long and tranquil existence, one must actively avoid unnecessary hazards and alluring dangers. Prudent individuals invariably evaluate every circumstance with meticulous care before committing to a definitive path. When unexpected crises emerge, even the most loyal allies may prove powerless to intervene. Consequently, remaining within a sphere of safety alongside those who share one own level of strength is infinitely preferable. Parents and mentors continue to recount this parable to equip children with the discernment required for survival. They desire that every growing mind comprehends the delicate balance between aspiration and capacity.

By listening attentively to these timeless traditions, individuals can navigate the treacherous currents of the future with greater wisdom. The memory of the two pots remains a potent symbol of consequence and reality. Life presents countless choices, demanding that every person selects companions who match their own physical and emotional fortitude. Those who fail to heed this guidance often find themselves overtaken by events they never anticipated. In the end, protection is not a gift bestowed by others, but an achievement rooted in self awareness.
